sections.heading: Kanyakumari — India's southern tip
bullets: Kanyakumari, in Tamil Nadu, is the southernmost town of mainland India; poets call it भारतमातुः चरणतीर्थम् — the holy place at Mother India's feet.
The lesson is a यात्रावर्णनम् (travel description) in original descriptive Sanskrit prose; the title राजते खलु कन्याकुमारी means 'Kanyakumari shines indeed'.
Thousands of travellers from India and abroad visit daily, drawn by the sea, the sights and the sacred associations.

sections.heading: The meeting of three seas
bullets: Three water bodies meet at Kanyakumari: the Bay of Bengal in the east, the Arabian Sea in the west and the Indian Ocean in the south.
The confluence is called त्रिवेणीसङ्गमः; standing on the shore one can even notice the differing colours of the waters.
Bathing at the confluence is believed by devotees to bestow merit (पुण्यप्रदम्); the foamy waves and their roar fill the shore.

sections.heading: Sunrise, sunset and the full-moon spectacle
bullets: At dawn the young sun (बालसूर्यः) rises from the 'womb of the sea', turning the water golden and the sky red.
Uniquely, both sunrise and sunset over the sea can be watched from the same shore.
On the Chaitra full moon (around April), the setting sun and the rising full moon can be seen at almost the same time in opposite directions.

sections.heading: Vivekananda Rock and the Thiruvalluvar statue
bullets: In December 1892 Swami Vivekananda swam to the offshore rock, meditated three days, and resolved to dedicate his life to India's uplift; in 1893 he addressed the World Parliament of Religions at Chicago.
The Vivekananda Rock Memorial, with its dhyana mandapam, was built on the rock in 1970; visitors reach it by boat.
The neighbouring statue of Thiruvalluvar, author of the Tirukkural, is 133 feet tall — one foot for each of the Tirukkural's 133 chapters — and was unveiled in 2000.

sections.heading: Temple, legend, unity — and grammar from the prose
bullets: The ancient temple of Devi Kanya Kumari, the maiden form of Parvati, gives the town its name; legend says her shining nose-ornament once guided boats at sea, and the Gandhi Mandapam stands nearby.
Kanyakumari symbolises India's unity: a southern goddess, a Tamil poet and a monk of Bengal honoured where three seas meet.

Grammar from the prose: गुण/दीर्घ सन्धि (सूर्योदयः, सूर्यास्तः, अतीव), compounds (सागरत्रयसङ्गमः, बालसूर्यः, देवीमन्दिरम्), कृदन्त forms (दृष्ट्वा, उपगम्य, द्रष्टुम्, निर्मितम्, रमणीयम्) and विभक्ति usage (नौकाभिः, तटात्, शिलायाम्).

key_takeaways: Kanyakumari in Tamil Nadu is the southernmost town of mainland India, where the land ends and three seas meet — hence राजते खलु कन्याकुमारी, 'Kanyakumari shines indeed'.
The Bay of Bengal (east), Arabian Sea (west) and Indian Ocean (south) form the सागरत्रयसङ्गम, popularly the Triveni Sangam, where the waters' colours visibly differ.
From one and the same shore both sunrise and sunset over the sea can be seen; on the Chaitra full moon, sunset and moonrise appear almost together.
Swami Vivekananda meditated on the offshore rock for three days in December 1892 and resolved to serve India; the Rock Memorial honouring him was built in 1970.
The Thiruvalluvar statue is 133 feet tall — matching the 133 chapters of the Tirukkural — and was unveiled in the year 2000.
The town is named after Devi Kanya Kumari, the maiden form of Parvati, whose ancient sea-shore temple and shining nose-ornament legend the lesson describes.
The prose teaches grammar in context: गुण-सन्धि in सूर्योदयः, दीर्घ-सन्धि in अतीव, compounds like सागरत्रयसङ्गमः, and कृदन्त forms like दृष्ट्वा, द्रष्टुम् and निर्मितम्.

glossary.definition: 'Shines, is resplendent' — from the root राज्; the verb of the title राजते खलु कन्याकुमारी.
An emphatic particle meaning 'indeed, certainly', adding wonder or affirmation to a statement.
A travel description — a prose composition describing a journey and the places seen, the literary form of this lesson.
The confluence of three seas — Bay of Bengal, Arabian Sea and Indian Ocean — meeting at Kanyakumari.
The Bay of Bengal, the sea to the east of Kanyakumari.
The Indian Ocean, the vast sea to the south of Kanyakumari.
Sunrise; formed by गुण-सन्धि from सूर्य + उदयः (अ + उ = ओ).
Sunset; formed by दीर्घ-सन्धि from सूर्य + अस्तः (अ + अ = आ).
The full-moon day; on the Chaitra full moon at Kanyakumari sunset and moonrise are seen almost together.
The offshore rock where Swami Vivekananda meditated for three days in December 1892; site of the 1970 Rock Memorial.
The celebrated Tamil book of ethics by Thiruvalluvar, containing 133 chapters — matched by the statue's 133-foot height.
A statue or image; here the 133-foot statue of Thiruvalluvar unveiled in 2000.
A nose-ornament; the Devi's nose-jewel whose radiance, legend says, was once visible to boats far out at sea.
A word derived from a verbal root by a कृत् suffix — e.g. दृष्ट्वा (having seen), द्रष्टुम् (to see), निर्मितम् (built).
A compound word; e.g. सागरत्रयसङ्गमः (तत्पुरुष on a द्विगु) and बालसूर्यः (कर्मधारय) from this lesson.

worksheet.title: Worksheet — राजते खलु कन्याकुमारी (NIOS Sanskrit 309, Chapter 6)
worksheet.instructions: Attempt all questions. Write Sanskrit words in Devanagari and give explanations in English where asked. Refer to the prose passage of the lesson where needed.

questions.question: कन्याकुमार्यां के त्रयः सागराः मिलन्ति? (Which three seas meet at Kanyakumari?)
options: Bay of Bengal, Arabian Sea, Indian Ocean
Bay of Bengal, Red Sea, Indian Ocean
Arabian Sea, Caspian Sea, Indian Ocean
Bay of Bengal, Arabian Sea, Pacific Ocean
questions.answer: Bay of Bengal, Arabian Sea, Indian Ocean
questions.explanation: पूर्वे बङ्गोपसागरः, पश्चिमे अरबसागरः, दक्षिणे हिन्दमहासागरः — the Bay of Bengal (east), Arabian Sea (west) and Indian Ocean (south) meet at Kanyakumari.

questions.question: The Thiruvalluvar statue is 133 feet tall because
questions.explanation: तस्मिन् ग्रन्थे १३३ अध्यायाः सन्ति — the statue's height matches the 133 chapters of the Tirukkural, one foot per chapter.

questions.question: स्वामी विवेकानन्दः १८९२ तमे वर्षे दिसम्बरमासे कन्याकुमार्याः शिलायां त्रिदिनं ध्यानम् अकरोत्। (Swami Vivekananda meditated for three days on the rock at Kanyakumari in December 1892.)
questions.explanation: The lesson records that Vivekananda swam to the rock in December 1892 and meditated there for three days, resolving to serve India.

questions.question: देव्याः ________ नाम्ना एव नगरस्य नाम 'कन्याकुमारी' इति अभवत्। (The town got its name from the goddess ________.)
questions.explanation: The town is named after Devi Kanya Kumari (कन्याकुमारी), the maiden form of Parvati worshipped in the sea-shore temple.

questions.question: सन्धि-विच्छेदं कुरुत, सन्धेः नाम अपि लिखत — (a) सूर्योदयः (b) अतीव. (Split the sandhi and name it.)
questions.answer: (a) सूर्योदयः = सूर्य + उदयः (अ + उ = ओ, गुण-सन्धिः). (b) अतीव = अति + इव (इ + इ = ई, दीर्घ-सन्धिः).
questions.explanation: गुण-सन्धि merges अ with उ into ओ; दीर्घ-सन्धि merges two similar short vowels into the long vowel.

questions.question: Give the शब्दार्थ (English meaning) of: यात्रिकाः, तीर्त्वा, औच्च्यम्, जनश्रुतिः.
questions.answer: यात्रिकाः = travellers/pilgrims; तीर्त्वा = having crossed (swum across); औच्च्यम् = height; जनश्रुतिः = popular tradition/legend.
questions.explanation: All four words occur in the prose passage — यात्रिकाः in the introduction, तीर्त्वा in the Vivekananda paragraph, औच्च्यम् in the statue paragraph, and जनश्रुतिः in the temple paragraph.

questions.question: Translate into English: 'एकस्मादेव तटात् सूर्योदयः सूर्यास्तः च द्रष्टुं शक्यते — इयम् एव कन्याकुमार्याः विशेषता।'
questions.answer: From one and the same shore both the sunrise and the sunset can be seen — this itself is the speciality of Kanyakumari.
questions.explanation: एकस्मादेव तटात् = from the very same shore (पञ्चमी); द्रष्टुं शक्यते = can be seen (तुमुन् infinitive with शक्); विशेषता = speciality.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer:
'सागरमध्ये एका महती शिला अस्ति। १८९२ तमे ख्रिष्टाब्दे स्वामी विवेकानन्दः सागरं तीर्त्वा तां शिलाम् उपगम्य त्रिदिनं ध्यानम् अकरोत्। तस्य स्मृत्यर्थं १९७० तमे वर्षे तत्र भव्यं शिलास्मारकं निर्मितम्।'
(a) विवेकानन्दः शिलायां किम् अकरोत्? (b) शिलास्मारकं कदा निर्मितम्? (c) Identify the two ल्यप्/क्त्वा (absolutive) forms in the passage.
questions.answer: (a) सः तत्र त्रिदिनं ध्यानम् अकरोत् — he meditated there for three days (in December 1892). (b) शिलास्मारकं १९७० तमे वर्षे निर्मितम् — the Rock Memorial was built in 1970. (c) The absolutives are तीर्त्वा (having crossed, क्त्वा) and उपगम्य (having approached, ल्यप् — used because of the prefix उप).
questions.explanation: The passage combines factual recall (three-day meditation, 1970 memorial) with grammar recognition of the two 'having done' forms.

questions.question: Write four simple Sanskrit sentences in Devanagari describing Kanyakumari (its location, the three seas, the sunrise, the statue). Give the English meaning of each.
questions.answer:
1. कन्याकुमारी भारतस्य दक्षिणतमे प्रान्ते अस्ति। (Kanyakumari is in the southernmost region of India.)
2. अत्र त्रयः सागराः मिलन्ति। (Here three seas meet.)
3. प्रातःकाले सूर्यः सागरात् उदेति। (In the morning the sun rises from the sea.)
4. तिरुवल्लुवरस्य उत्तुङ्गा प्रतिमा सागरमध्ये राजते। (The lofty statue of Thiruvalluvar shines in the midst of the sea.)
questions.explanation: Simple प्रथमा-subject sentences using chapter vocabulary — अस्ति, मिलन्ति, उदेति, राजते — covering location, confluence, sunrise and the statue.

questions.question: 'कन्याकुमारी भारतस्य एकतायाः प्रतीकम्' — Kanyakumari is a symbol of India's unity. Explain this statement in about 100-120 words using at least three examples from the lesson.
questions.answer: The lesson closes by calling Kanyakumari not merely a place of natural beauty but a symbol (प्रतीकम्) of India's unity. Three examples support this. First, geography itself unites here: three different seas — the Bay of Bengal, the Arabian Sea and the Indian Ocean — merge into one confluence (सागरत्रयसङ्गमः). Second, the shore brings together the ancient temple of a southern goddess (देवी कन्याकुमारी), the towering statue of the Tamil poet Thiruvalluvar, and the memorial of Swami Vivekananda, a monk from Bengal in India's east — south and north, poet and saint, honoured side by side. Third, pilgrims and travellers from every state and from abroad gather daily on the same shore. As the seas merge, so do India's regions, languages and traditions — therefore राजते खलु कन्याकुमारी.
questions.explanation: A model senior-secondary answer: states the claim, gives the geographic, cultural and human examples, and ties back to the title.

questions.question: कन्याकुमारी कस्मिन् राज्ये अस्ति? (Kanyakumari is in which state?)
questions.explanation: The lesson opens: भारतवर्षस्य दक्षिणतमे प्रान्ते तमिळनाडुराज्ये कन्याकुमारी नाम नगरम् अस्ति — Kanyakumari is in Tamil Nadu.

questions.question: 'राजते खलु कन्याकुमारी' इत्यत्र 'राजते' इत्यस्य कः अर्थः?
questions.explanation: राजते comes from the root राज् 'to shine'; the title means 'Kanyakumari shines indeed'. It does not mean 'rules' here.

questions.question: अस्मिन् पाठे 'खलु' इति अव्ययस्य अर्थः कः?
questions.explanation: खलु is an emphatic particle meaning 'indeed/certainly', expressing the traveller's wonder in the title.

questions.question: This lesson belongs to which literary form?
questions.explanation: The chapter is a यात्रावर्णनम् — descriptive travel prose about Kanyakumari, not a drama, champu or hymn.

questions.question: कविभिः कन्याकुमारी किम् इति वर्ण्यते?
questions.explanation: Poets call Kanyakumari 'भारतमातुः चरणतीर्थम्' — the holy tirtha at the feet of Mother India, since the land ends there.

questions.question: 'भारतमातुः चरणतीर्थम्' — Kanyakumari is at Mother India's FEET because
options: it lies at the southernmost tip where the mainland ends
the goddess's feet are worshipped there
it is the lowest place below sea level in India
questions.answer: it lies at the southernmost tip where the mainland ends
questions.explanation: If India is pictured as a standing figure, the Himalayas are the head and Kanyakumari, the southernmost point of the mainland, is at the feet — अत्र एव भारतभूमिः समाप्यते.

questions.question: Kanyakumari was formerly known to Europeans by which name?
questions.explanation: Kanyakumari was called Cape Comorin in colonial usage; the name derives from Kanya Kumari, the virgin goddess.

questions.question: 'देश-विदेशेभ्यः सहस्रशः यात्रिकाः आगच्छन्ति' — इत्यत्र 'सहस्रशः' इत्यस्य अर्थः कः?
questions.explanation: The suffix -शः gives a distributive/multitude sense: सहस्रशः = by the thousands. Thousands of travellers arrive daily.

questions.question: 'अत्र एव भारतभूमिः समाप्यते, सागरः च आरभ्यते' — the pair समाप्यते/आरभ्यते conveys which idea?
options: the land ends and the ocean begins at this very spot
the journey ends and a festival begins
the day ends and night begins
the temple closes and the fair begins
questions.answer: the land ends and the ocean begins at this very spot
questions.explanation: समाप्यते = 'is completed/ends', आरभ्यते = 'begins' — at Kanyakumari the Indian mainland ends and the sea begins.

questions.question: कन्याकुमार्यां कति सागराः मिलन्ति?
questions.explanation: Three seas meet at Kanyakumari — the Bay of Bengal, the Arabian Sea and the Indian Ocean (सागरत्रयसङ्गमः).

questions.question: पूर्वस्यां दिशि कः सागरः अस्ति?
questions.explanation: To the east of Kanyakumari lies the Bay of Bengal; the Arabian Sea is to the west and the Indian Ocean to the south.

questions.question: दक्षिणस्यां दिशि कः महासागरः विद्यते?
questions.explanation: The vast Indian Ocean (विशालः हिन्दमहासागरः) lies to the south of Kanyakumari.

questions.question: सागरत्रयस्य सङ्गमः केन नाम्ना प्रसिद्धः?
questions.explanation: The meeting of the three seas at Kanyakumari is popularly called the त्रिवेणीसङ्गम (Triveni Sangam), on the model of the three-river confluence.

questions.question: तटे स्थित्वा सागराणां किं द्रष्टुं शक्यते इति पाठे उक्तम्?
options: जलानां वर्णभेदः (difference in the colours of the waters)
questions.answer: जलानां वर्णभेदः (difference in the colours of the waters)
questions.explanation: आश्चर्यम् इदं यत् त्रयाणां सागराणां जलानां वर्णभेदः अपि द्रष्टुं शक्यते — the colour difference of the three seas' waters is visible from the shore.

questions.question: भक्तानां विश्वासः अस्ति यत् सङ्गमस्नानं ________ भवति।
questions.explanation: सङ्गमस्नानं पुण्यप्रदम् इति भक्तानां विश्वासः — devotees believe bathing at the confluence bestows merit (पुण्य).

questions.question: 'तरङ्गाः तटम् आहत्य फेनिलाः भवन्ति' — अस्य वाक्यस्य समीचीनः अनुवादः कः?
options: The waves strike the shore and become foamy
The waves avoid the shore and become calm
The boats strike the shore and break
The winds strike the waves and stop
questions.answer: The waves strike the shore and become foamy
questions.explanation: तरङ्गाः = waves; आहत्य = having struck (ल्यप्); फेनिलाः = foamy. The waves strike the shore and turn foamy.

questions.question: Why is the name 'त्रिवेणीसङ्गमः' apt for Kanyakumari even though no rivers meet there?
options: Because three great water bodies merge there, like the three rivers at Prayag
Because three rivers of Tamil Nadu end there
Because the goddess has three names
Because three mountains meet the sea there
questions.answer: Because three great water bodies merge there, like the three rivers at Prayag
questions.explanation: The classic त्रिवेणी is the three-river confluence at Prayag; Kanyakumari borrows the name because three SEAS — Bay of Bengal, Arabian Sea, Indian Ocean — merge there.

questions.question: 'तेषां घोषः दूरात् अपि श्रूयते' — इत्यत्र 'घोषः' कस्य अस्ति?
questions.explanation: तेषाम् refers back to the waves (तरङ्गाः) that strike the shore — their roar (घोषः) is heard even from afar.

questions.question: पश्चिमायां दिशि कः सागरः अस्ति?
questions.explanation: The Arabian Sea lies to the west (पश्चिमायां दिशि) of Kanyakumari.

questions.question: प्रातःकाले सूर्यः कुतः उदेति इति पाठे वर्णितम्?
options: सागरगर्भात् (from the womb of the sea)
questions.answer: सागरगर्भात् (from the womb of the sea)
questions.explanation: बालसूर्यः सागरगर्भात् शनैः शनैः उदेति — the young sun rises slowly from the 'womb of the sea'.

questions.question: सूर्योदयकाले जलं कीदृशं भवति?
questions.explanation: तदा जलं सुवर्णवर्णं भवति, आकाशः च रक्तवर्णः — at sunrise the water turns golden and the sky red.

questions.question: कन्याकुमार्याः 'विशेषता' का इति पाठे उक्तम्?
options: एकस्मादेव तटात् सूर्योदयः सूर्यास्तः च दृश्येते
तत्र सूर्यः कदापि न अस्तं गच्छति
तत्र सूर्यः पूर्वस्यां दिशि अस्तं गच्छति
questions.answer: एकस्मादेव तटात् सूर्योदयः सूर्यास्तः च दृश्येते
questions.explanation: The unique feature (विशेषता) is that both sunrise and sunset over the sea can be watched from one and the same shore.

questions.question: कस्यां पूर्णिमायां सूर्यास्तः चन्द्रोदयः च युगपत् इव दृश्येते?
questions.explanation: On the Chaitra full moon (around April), the setting sun and the rising full moon are seen almost simultaneously in opposite directions.

questions.question: 'सः एव सूर्यः पश्चिमसागरे मज्जति इव दृश्यते' — 'मज्जति' इत्यस्य अर्थः कः?
questions.explanation: मज्जति (root मस्ज्) = sinks/dives; at sunset the sun seems to sink into the western sea. इव marks the poetic comparison.

questions.question: 'शनैः शनैः' इत्यस्य अर्थः कः?
questions.explanation: The repeated adverb शनैः शनैः means 'slowly, step by step' — the young sun rises gradually from the sea.

questions.question: चैत्रपूर्णिमायाः दृश्यं किमर्थम् 'अद्भुतम्' इति कथ्यते?
options: यतः एकस्यां दिशि सूर्यः अस्तं गच्छति, अन्यस्यां च पूर्णचन्द्रः उदेति
यतः तस्मिन् दिने सागरः शान्तः भवति
यतः तस्मिन् दिने त्रयः सूर्याः दृश्यन्ते
यतः तस्मिन् दिने चन्द्रः रक्तवर्णः भवति
questions.answer: यतः एकस्यां दिशि सूर्यः अस्तं गच्छति, अन्यस्यां च पूर्णचन्द्रः उदेति
questions.explanation: The wonder is the simultaneity: the sun sets in one direction while the full moon rises in the other — visible together from the same shore.

questions.question: 'एतत् दृश्यं दृष्ट्वा यात्रिकाः विस्मिताः भवन्ति' — 'विस्मिताः' means
questions.explanation: विस्मित (क्त participle of वि + स्मि) = amazed. Seeing the spectacle, travellers are filled with wonder — not fear or fatigue.

questions.question: सूर्योदयकाले आकाशः कीदृशः भवति?
questions.explanation: At sunrise the water turns golden (सुवर्णवर्णम्) and the sky red (रक्तवर्णः), as described in the third paragraph.

questions.question: स्वामी विवेकानन्दः कस्मिन् वर्षे कन्याकुमार्याः शिलायां ध्यानम् अकरोत्?
questions.explanation: Vivekananda reached the rock in December 1892 and meditated there for three days; the Chicago address followed in 1893.

questions.question: विवेकानन्दः शिलायां कति दिनानि ध्यानम् अकरोत्?
questions.explanation: सः तां शिलाम् उपगम्य त्रिदिनं ध्यानम् अकरोत् — he meditated on the rock for three days in December 1892.

questions.question: विवेकानन्दशिलायां भव्यं शिलास्मारकं कदा निर्मितम्?
questions.explanation: The Vivekananda Rock Memorial was built on the rock in 1970, in memory of the swami's 1892 meditation.

questions.question: विवेकानन्दः १८९३ तमे वर्षे कुत्र विश्वधर्मसम्मेलने भाषणम् अकरोत्?
questions.explanation: In 1893 Vivekananda addressed the World Parliament of Religions (विश्वधर्मसम्मेलनम्) at Chicago, carrying India's message to the world.

questions.question: शिलायां ध्यानं कुर्वन् विवेकानन्दः कं निश्चयम् अकरोत्?
questions.explanation: On the rock he resolved to dedicate his life to the uplift (उत्थानम्) of India — the turning point of his mission.

questions.question: विवेकानन्दः शिलां कथं प्राप्तवान् इति पाठे सूचितम्?
options: सागरं तीर्त्वा (by swimming across the sea)
questions.answer: सागरं तीर्त्वा (by swimming across the sea)
questions.explanation: सः सागरं तीर्त्वा तां शिलाम् उपगम्य — he crossed (swam) the sea to reach the rock; there was no bridge or boat for him.

questions.question: अद्य यात्रिकाः विवेकानन्दशिलां कथं गच्छन्ति?
questions.explanation: यात्रिकाः नौकाभिः तत्र गत्वा ध्यानमण्डपे शान्तिम् अनुभवन्ति — visitors today reach the Rock Memorial by ferry boats.

questions.question: Why is December 1892 considered a turning point in Vivekananda's life?
options: On the rock he resolved to dedicate himself to India's uplift, which led to his world mission
He first became a sannyasi in that month
He met Sri Ramakrishna there for the first time
He founded the Ramakrishna Mission on the rock that month
questions.answer: On the rock he resolved to dedicate himself to India's uplift, which led to his world mission
questions.explanation: The three-day meditation ended his wandering years with a clear resolve to serve India — the resolve that carried him to Chicago in 1893. He had met Ramakrishna years earlier, and the Mission was founded in 1897 at Calcutta.

questions.question: 'तस्य स्मृत्यर्थं शिलास्मारकं निर्मितम्' — 'स्मृत्यर्थम्' इत्यस्य अर्थः कः?
questions.explanation: स्मृति (memory) + अर्थम् (for the sake of) = 'for the sake of memory, in memory of'. The memorial commemorates Vivekananda.

questions.question: यात्रिकाः ध्यानमण्डपे किम् अनुभवन्ति इति पाठे उक्तम्, तत् किं सूचयति?
options: शान्तिम् — the place still carries the meditative stillness of Vivekananda's tapasya
भयम् — the sea frightens the visitors
क्लेशम् — the journey by boat is difficult
शीतम् — the hall is very cold
questions.answer: शान्तिम् — the place still carries the meditative stillness of Vivekananda's tapasya
questions.explanation: Visitors experience peace (शान्तिः) in the dhyana mandapam — the text suggests the rock remains a place of meditation, continuing Vivekananda's legacy.

questions.question: तिरुवल्लुवरः कस्य ग्रन्थस्य रचयिता?
questions.explanation: Thiruvalluvar is the celebrated author of the Tirukkural, the Tamil classic on ethics (नीतिग्रन्थः).

questions.question: तिरुवल्लुवर-प्रतिमायाः औच्च्यं कियत्?
questions.explanation: The statue is 133 feet (about 41 metres) tall — one foot for each of the 133 chapters of the Tirukkural.

questions.question: तिरुक्कुरळ्-ग्रन्थे कति अध्यायाः सन्ति?
questions.explanation: The Tirukkural has 133 chapters (अध्यायाः); the statue's 133-foot height honours this number.

questions.question: तिरुवल्लुवर-प्रतिमा कस्मिन् वर्षे अनावृता?
questions.explanation: The Thiruvalluvar statue was unveiled to the public on 1 January 2000.

questions.question: तिरुवल्लुवरः कस्याः भाषायाः महाकविः?
questions.explanation: Thiruvalluvar is the great poet-saint of Tamil (तमिळमहाकविः); the Tirukkural is a jewel of Tamil literature.

questions.question: 'तिरुक्कुरळ्' कीदृशः ग्रन्थः इति पाठे उक्तम्?
questions.explanation: The Tirukkural is described as a नीतिग्रन्थः — a work of ethics and right conduct, treating virtue, wealth and love.

questions.question: दूरात् दृष्टा तिरुवल्लुवर-प्रतिमा कस्य इव प्रतिभाति?
options: धर्मस्य प्रहरी इव (like a sentinel of dharma)
सागरस्य राजा इव (like a king of the sea)
पर्वतस्य शिखरम् इव (like a mountain peak)
questions.answer: धर्मस्य प्रहरी इव (like a sentinel of dharma)
questions.explanation: दूरात् दृष्टा सा प्रतिमा धर्मस्य प्रहरी इव प्रतिभाति — seen from afar, the statue appears like a sentinel of dharma standing in the sea.

questions.question: प्रतिमायाः औच्च्यं १३३ पादमितम् इति सङ्ख्या किं सूचयति?
options: ग्रन्थस्य अध्यायसङ्ख्यां — the form of the statue honours the content of the book
कवेः आयुः — the poet lived 133 years
शिलायाः भारम् — the rock weighs 133 tonnes
नगरस्य वयः — the town is 133 years old
questions.answer: ग्रन्थस्य अध्यायसङ्ख्यां — the form of the statue honours the content of the book
questions.explanation: The 133 feet deliberately mirror the Tirukkural's 133 chapters — architecture encoding literature: the monument honours the WORK, not merely the man.

questions.question: तिरुवल्लुवर-प्रतिमा कुत्र स्थिता?
questions.explanation: The statue stands on another offshore rock near the Vivekananda Rock — the two monuments are neighbours in the sea.

questions.question: नगरस्य नाम 'कन्याकुमारी' इति कस्याः नाम्ना अभवत्?
questions.explanation: तस्याः देव्याः नाम्ना एव नगरस्य नाम अभवत् — the town takes its name from Goddess Kanya Kumari of the sea-shore temple.

questions.question: देवी कन्याकुमारी कस्याः देव्याः रूपम् इति भक्ताः विश्वसन्ति?
questions.explanation: देवी कन्याकुमारी पार्वत्याः एव कन्यारूपम् — devotees regard the goddess as the maiden form of Parvati.

questions.question: मन्दिरे देव्याः मूर्तिः हस्ते किं धारयति?
questions.explanation: मूर्तिः हस्ते जपमालां धारयति — in the temple the goddess's image holds a japa-mala (rosary) in her hand.

questions.question: जनश्रुतिः का अस्ति देव्याः नासाभरणविषये?
options: तस्य प्रभा सागरे दूरं गच्छन्तीभिः नौकाभिः अपि दृश्यते स्म
questions.answer: तस्य प्रभा सागरे दूरं गच्छन्तीभिः नौकाभिः अपि दृश्यते स्म
questions.explanation: Legend (जनश्रुतिः) says the nose-ornament shone so brightly that its radiance was once visible even to boats far out at sea.

questions.question: गान्धीमण्डपे किं स्थापितम् आसीत्?
options: गान्धिनः प्रतिमा एव केवलम् (only Gandhi's statue)
questions.explanation: यत्र महात्मगान्धिनः भस्म स्थापितम् आसीत् — the Gandhi Mandapam on the shore preserved Gandhi's ashes before their immersion in the sea.

questions.question: पाठस्य उपसंहारे कन्याकुमारी कस्य 'प्रतीकम्' इति उक्ता?
options: सागरशक्तेः (of the power of the sea)
questions.explanation: कन्याकुमारी ... भारतस्य एकतायाः प्रतीकम् — the conclusion presents Kanyakumari as a symbol of India's unity.

questions.question: उपसंहारे 'यथा त्रयः सागराः एकत्र मिलन्ति तथा' इति उपमा किं सूचयति?
options: यथा सागराः मिलन्ति तथा भारतस्य विविधाः संस्कृतयः अपि अत्र मिलन्ति
यथा सागराः मिलन्ति तथा नद्यः अपि मिलन्ति
यथा सागराः गर्जन्ति तथा जनाः अपि गर्जन्ति
यथा सागराः विशालाः तथा मन्दिरम् अपि विशालम्
questions.answer: यथा सागराः मिलन्ति तथा भारतस्य विविधाः संस्कृतयः अपि अत्र मिलन्ति
questions.explanation: The simile compares the physical merging of three seas with the cultural meeting of south (Devi temple, Tamil poet) and north/east (the monk of Bengal) — India's diversity uniting at one point.

questions.question: देवीमन्दिरं कुत्र स्थितम्?
options: सागरमध्ये शिलायाम् (on a rock in the sea)
नगरात् दूरे वने (in a forest far from town)
questions.explanation: सागरतटे देव्याः प्राचीनं मन्दिरम् अस्ति — the ancient temple stands on the shore, unlike the rock memorial and the statue which stand in the sea.

questions.question: पाठे भारतस्य एकतायाः कृते कानि त्रीणि स्थलानि 'एकत्र मिलन्ति' इति उक्तानि?
questions.explanation: The southern goddess's temple, the Tamil poet's statue and the memorial of the monk of Bengal (Vivekananda) stand together — like the three seas.

questions.question: 'सूर्योदयः' इत्यस्य सन्धि-विच्छेदः कः?
questions.explanation: सूर्य + उदयः = सूर्योदयः; the final अ and initial उ merge into ओ by गुण-सन्धि.

questions.question: 'सूर्योदयः' इत्यत्र कः सन्धिः?
questions.explanation: When अ/आ meets उ/ऊ the result is ओ — गुण-सन्धिः, as in सूर्य + उदयः = सूर्योदयः and चन्द्र + उदयः = चन्द्रोदयः.

questions.question: 'सूर्यास्तः' इत्यस्य सन्धि-विच्छेदः कः?
questions.explanation: सूर्य + अस्तः = सूर्यास्तः; अ + अ merge into long आ — दीर्घ-सन्धिः.

questions.question: 'अतीव' इति पदं कयोः पदयोः सन्धिना निष्पन्नम्?
questions.explanation: अति + इव = अतीव; इ + इ merge into long ई by दीर्घ-सन्धिः.

questions.question: 'सागरत्रयसङ्गमः' इति समासस्य विग्रहः कः?
options: सागरः च त्रयः च सङ्गमः च
questions.explanation: सागरत्रयसङ्गमः = सागरत्रयस्य सङ्गमः (the confluence OF the triad of seas) — a षष्ठी-तत्पुरुष built on the द्विगु compound सागरत्रयम्.

questions.question: 'बालसूर्यः' (the young sun) — अयं कः समासः?
questions.explanation: बालः च असौ सूर्यः च = बालसूर्यः — adjective + noun in apposition is a कर्मधारय compound.

questions.question: 'द्रष्टुम्' (to see) इति पदे कः कृत्-प्रत्ययः?
questions.explanation: द्रष्टुम् is the infinitive 'to see' formed with the तुमुन् suffix (दृश् + तुमुन्), as in द्रष्टुं शक्यते 'can be seen'.

questions.question: 'उपगम्य' (having approached) इति पदे कः प्रत्ययः, किमर्थं च?
options: ल्यप् — यतः धातोः पूर्वम् उपसर्गः अस्ति
questions.answer: ल्यप् — यतः धातोः पूर्वम् उपसर्गः अस्ति
questions.explanation: With a prefix (उप + गम्), the absolutive takes ल्यप् (-य): उपगम्य. Without a prefix it takes क्त्वा, e.g. गत्वा, दृष्ट्वा.

questions.question: 'नौकाभिः' इति पदे का विभक्तिः?
questions.explanation: नौकाभिः = 'by boats' — तृतीया (instrumental) plural of नौका, showing the means of travel.

questions.question: 'निर्मितम्' (was built) इति पदे कः प्रत्ययः?
questions.explanation: निर्मितम् (निर् + मा/मि + क्त) is a past passive participle — 'built/constructed', as in शिलास्मारकं निर्मितम्.

questions.question: 'यात्रिकाः' इत्यस्य शब्दार्थः कः?
questions.explanation: यात्रिकाः (from यात्रा, journey) = travellers or pilgrims — those who come to see Kanyakumari.

questions.question: 'उत्तुङ्गा' इत्यस्य शब्दार्थः कः?
questions.explanation: उत्तुङ्ग = lofty/towering; the Thiruvalluvar statue is described as उत्तुङ्गा प्रतिमा.

questions.question: 'जनश्रुतिः' इत्यस्य समीचीनः अर्थः कः?
questions.explanation: जनश्रुतिः = 'what is heard among the people' — a popular tradition or legend, like the tale of the shining nose-ornament.

questions.question: 'पुण्यप्रदम्' इत्यस्य अर्थः कः?
questions.explanation: पुण्य (merit) + प्रद (giving) = पुण्यप्रदम्, 'that which bestows merit' — said of bathing at the confluence.

questions.question: 'ते सर्वे एकस्वरेण वदन्ति' — अस्य समीचीनः अनुवादः कः?
options: They all say with one voice
They each speak a different language
questions.answer: They all say with one voice
questions.explanation: एकस्वरेण (तृतीया) = 'with one voice, unanimously'; the travellers unanimously declare — राजते खलु कन्याकुमारी!

questions.question: 'सागरतटे देव्याः प्राचीनं मन्दिरम् अस्ति' — अस्य वाक्यस्य अनुवादः कः?
options: On the sea-shore there is an ancient temple of the goddess
In the sea there is a new temple of the goddess
On the shore the goddess builds a temple
The ancient goddess lives near the temple
questions.answer: On the sea-shore there is an ancient temple of the goddess
questions.explanation: सागरतटे (सप्तमी, 'on the shore'), देव्याः (षष्ठी, 'of the goddess'), प्राचीनम् = ancient — a straightforward locative sentence.

questions.question: 'प्रहरी इव प्रतिभाति' — इत्यत्र 'इव' इति अव्ययं किं कार्यं करोति?
questions.explanation: इव marks a simile: the statue appears LIKE a sentinel (प्रहरी इव). The particle signals comparison, a key device of descriptive prose.

questions.question: 'भस्म' इत्यस्य शब्दार्थः कः?
questions.explanation: भस्म = ashes; Mahatma Gandhi's ashes (भस्म) were kept at the Gandhi Mandapam before immersion in the sea.

questions.question: यात्रावर्णने लेखकः वर्णनं जीवन्तं कर्तुं कानि साधनानि प्रयुङ्क्ते इति अस्मात् पाठात् ज्ञायते?
options: वर्णचित्रणम्, उपमाः, कृदन्तपदानि च (colour imagery, similes and participles)
questions.answer: वर्णचित्रणम्, उपमाः, कृदन्तपदानि च (colour imagery, similes and participles)
questions.explanation: The prose paints colours (सुवर्णवर्णं जलम्, रक्तवर्णः आकाशः), uses similes (मज्जति इव, प्रहरी इव) and strings of participles (दृष्ट्वा, तीर्त्वा, उपगम्य) — the marks of vivid यात्रावर्णन style.

questions.question: कन्याकुमारी भारतस्य उत्तरतमे प्रान्ते अस्ति। (Kanyakumari is in the northernmost region of India.)
questions.explanation: False — Kanyakumari is in the SOUTHERNMOST (दक्षिणतमे) region of mainland India, in Tamil Nadu, not the north.

questions.question: कन्याकुमार्यां बङ्गोपसागरः, अरबसागरः, हिन्दमहासागरः च मिलन्ति। (The Bay of Bengal, the Arabian Sea and the Indian Ocean meet at Kanyakumari.)
questions.explanation: True — the three seas meet at Kanyakumari, forming the सागरत्रयसङ्गम known as the Triveni Sangam.

questions.question: अरबसागरः कन्याकुमार्याः पूर्वस्यां दिशि अस्ति। (The Arabian Sea lies to the east of Kanyakumari.)
questions.explanation: False — the Arabian Sea lies to the WEST (पश्चिमायां दिशि); the Bay of Bengal is to the east.

questions.question: कन्याकुमार्याम् एकस्मादेव तटात् सूर्योदयः सूर्यास्तः च द्रष्टुं शक्यते। (At Kanyakumari both sunrise and sunset can be seen from the same shore.)
questions.explanation: True — this is the special glory (विशेषता) of Kanyakumari: both sunrise and sunset over the sea are visible from one shore.

questions.question: विवेकानन्दशिलायाः स्मारकं १८९३ तमे वर्षे निर्मितम्। (The Vivekananda Rock Memorial was built in 1893.)
questions.explanation: False — the memorial was built in 1970. 1893 is the year of Vivekananda's Chicago address; his meditation on the rock was in December 1892.

questions.question: स्वामी विवेकानन्दः सागरं तीर्त्वा शिलां प्राप्तवान्। (Swami Vivekananda reached the rock by swimming across the sea.)
questions.explanation: True — the lesson says सः सागरं तीर्त्वा तां शिलाम् उपगम्य; he swam across to the rock in December 1892.

questions.question: तिरुवल्लुवर-प्रतिमायाः औच्च्यं तिरुक्कुरळ्-ग्रन्थस्य अध्यायसङ्ख्यानुसारं १३३ पादमितम् अस्ति। (The Thiruvalluvar statue is 133 feet tall, matching the number of chapters of the Tirukkural.)
questions.explanation: True — the Tirukkural has 133 chapters, and the statue's height was fixed at 133 feet in their honour; it was unveiled in 2000.

questions.question: देवी कन्याकुमारी लक्ष्म्याः रूपम् इति भक्ताः विश्वसन्ति। (Devotees believe Devi Kanya Kumari is a form of Lakshmi.)
questions.explanation: False — the lesson says देवी कन्याकुमारी पार्वत्याः एव कन्यारूपम्: she is believed to be the maiden form of PARVATI, not Lakshmi.

questions.question: 'अतीव' इति पदं दीर्घ-सन्धेः उदाहरणम् अस्ति। ('अतीव' is an example of दीर्घ-सन्धि.)
questions.explanation: True — अति + इव = अतीव: the two short इ vowels merge into long ई, which is दीर्घ-सन्धिः.

questions.question: 'फेनिलाः' इत्यस्य अर्थः 'foamy' इति अस्ति। (The word 'फेनिलाः' means 'foamy'.)
questions.explanation: True — फेनिल (from फेन, foam) = foamy; the waves striking the shore become foamy (फेनिलाः भवन्ति).

questions.question: भारतवर्षस्य ________ प्रान्ते तमिळनाडुराज्ये कन्याकुमारी नगरम् अस्ति। (Kanyakumari is in the ________ region of India.)
questions.explanation: दक्षिणतमे = 'in the southernmost' — Kanyakumari lies at the southernmost tip of mainland India.

questions.question: राजते ________ कन्याकुमारी! (Complete the title of the lesson with the emphatic particle.)
questions.explanation: The title is राजते खलु कन्याकुमारी — 'Kanyakumari shines indeed'; खलु is the emphatic particle.

questions.question: कन्याकुमार्यां ________ सागराः मिलन्ति। (At Kanyakumari ________ seas meet — write the Sanskrit number word.)
questions.explanation: त्रयः (three) — the Bay of Bengal, the Arabian Sea and the Indian Ocean meet at Kanyakumari.

questions.question: सागरत्रयस्य सङ्गमः '________-सङ्गमः' इति कथ्यते। (The confluence of the three seas is called the ________ Sangam.)
questions.explanation: The confluence is popularly called त्रिवेणीसङ्गमः (Triveni Sangam), on the model of the three-river confluence at Prayag.

questions.question: प्रातःकाले बालसूर्यः ________ शनैः शनैः उदेति। (In the morning the young sun rises slowly from the ________ — one Sanskrit word, ablative.)
questions.explanation: सागरगर्भात् = 'from the womb of the sea' (पञ्चमी) — the poetic image of the sun rising out of the ocean.

questions.question: स्वामी विवेकानन्दः शिलायां त्रिदिनं ________ अकरोत्। (On the rock Swami Vivekananda performed ________ for three days.)
questions.explanation: ध्यानम् = meditation; he meditated on the rock for three days in December 1892.

questions.question: १८९३ तमे वर्षे विवेकानन्दः चिकागोनगरे ________ भारतीयसंस्कृतेः सन्देशम् अददात्। (In 1893, at the World Parliament of Religions in Chicago — fill the Sanskrit locative compound.)
questions.explanation: विश्वधर्मसम्मेलने = 'at the World Parliament of Religions' (सप्तमी); there he gave India's message to the world.

questions.question: तिरुवल्लुवरः '________' इति नीतिग्रन्थस्य रचयिता। (Thiruvalluvar is the author of the ethics classic ________.)
questions.explanation: The Tirukkural (तिरुक्कुरळ्), with its 133 chapters, is Thiruvalluvar's celebrated book of ethics.

questions.question: तिरुवल्लुवरस्य उत्तुङ्गा ________ सागरमध्ये राजते। (Thiruvalluvar's lofty ________ shines in the midst of the sea.)
questions.explanation: प्रतिमा = statue; the 133-foot statue of Thiruvalluvar stands on a rock in the sea near the Vivekananda Rock.

questions.question: मन्दिरे देव्याः मूर्तिः हस्ते ________ धारयति। (In the temple the goddess's image holds a ________ in her hand.)
questions.explanation: जपमालाम् (द्वितीया of जपमाला) = rosary; the image of Devi Kanya Kumari holds a japa-mala.

questions.question: सन्धिं कुरुत: सूर्य + उदयः = ________
questions.explanation: सूर्य + उदयः = सूर्योदयः by गुण-सन्धि (अ + उ = ओ).

questions.question: सन्धिं कुरुत: चन्द्र + उदयः = ________
questions.explanation: चन्द्र + उदयः = चन्द्रोदयः by गुण-सन्धि (अ + उ = ओ), exactly parallel to सूर्योदयः.

questions.question: 'गम्' धातोः क्त्वा-प्रत्ययान्तं रूपं लिखत (having gone): ________
questions.explanation: गम् + क्त्वा = गत्वा 'having gone', as in नौकाभिः तत्र गत्वा — 'having gone there by boats'.

questions.question: 'औच्च्यम्' इत्यस्य आङ्ग्लभाषायाम् अर्थः ________ इति। (The English meaning of औच्च्यम् is ________.)
questions.explanation: औच्च्यम् (from उच्च, high) = height; the statue's height is 133 feet.

questions.question: सूर्योदयकाले जलं ________ भवति। (At sunrise the water becomes ________-coloured — one Sanskrit word from the text.)
questions.explanation: सुवर्णवर्णम् = golden-coloured; the dawn sea turns golden while the sky turns red (रक्तवर्णः).

questions.question: 'राजते खलु कन्याकुमारी' — पाठशीर्षकस्य अर्थं लिखत। (Explain the meaning of the lesson's title.)
questions.answer: The title means 'Kanyakumari shines indeed!'. राजते (from root राज्) means 'shines, is resplendent', and खलु is an emphatic particle meaning 'indeed, certainly'. The title voices the traveller's wonder at the beauty of Kanyakumari — its seas, sunrises, monuments and temple.
questions.explanation: Tests understanding of the verb राजते and the particle खलु and the mood of the यात्रावर्णन.

questions.question: कन्याकुमारी 'भारतमातुः चरणतीर्थम्' इति किमर्थं कथ्यते? (Why is Kanyakumari called the holy place at Mother India's feet?)
questions.answer: Because Kanyakumari lies at the southernmost tip of mainland India — the very point where the land of India ends and the ocean begins (अत्र एव भारतभूमिः समाप्यते, सागरः च आरभ्यते). If India is imagined as Mother Bharata standing with the Himalayas as her crown, Kanyakumari is at her feet; hence poets call it her चरणतीर्थम्, the sacred spot at her feet.
questions.explanation: Requires connecting the geographic fact (southernmost point) with the poetic image of भारतमाता.

questions.question: कन्याकुमार्यां मिलतां त्रयाणां सागराणां नामानि दिशः च लिखत। (Name the three seas that meet at Kanyakumari, with their directions.)
questions.answer: पूर्वस्यां दिशि बङ्गोपसागरः (Bay of Bengal in the east), पश्चिमायां दिशि अरबसागरः (Arabian Sea in the west), दक्षिणस्यां दिशि च हिन्दमहासागरः (Indian Ocean in the south).
questions.explanation: Direct recall of the सागरत्रयसङ्गम paragraph — three seas with their directions.

questions.question: सङ्गमस्थाने तटे स्थित्वा किम् आश्चर्यं द्रष्टुं शक्यते? भक्ताः च सङ्गमस्नानविषये किं विश्वसन्ति? (What wonder can be seen from the shore at the confluence, and what do devotees believe about bathing there?)
questions.answer: Standing on the shore one can see the difference in the colours of the waters (जलानां वर्णभेदः) of the three seas — an astonishing sight. Devotees believe that bathing at the confluence bestows merit (सङ्गमस्नानं पुण्यप्रदम् इति भक्तानां विश्वासः).
questions.explanation: Two facts from the second paragraph: the visible colour difference and the belief in merit-giving bath.

questions.question: 'त्रिवेणीसङ्गमः' इति नाम प्रयागस्य नदीसङ्गमात् कथं भिन्नम्, कथं च समानम्? (How is the 'Triveni Sangam' of Kanyakumari different from and similar to the river confluence at Prayag?)
questions.answer: Similarity: in both, three waters merge at one holy point, and bathing at the confluence is considered merit-giving. Difference: at Prayag three RIVERS (Ganga, Yamuna and the invisible Sarasvati) meet inland, while at Kanyakumari three SEAS — the Bay of Bengal, the Arabian Sea and the Indian Ocean — meet at the ocean's edge. The name त्रिवेणीसङ्गमः is thus applied to Kanyakumari by analogy.
questions.explanation: An analysis question comparing the classical Triveni with the sea-confluence; tests transfer of the concept.

questions.question: सूर्योदयकाले कन्याकुमार्यां किं किं दृश्यते इति पाठानुसारं लिखत। (Describe, following the text, what is seen at sunrise at Kanyakumari.)
questions.answer: At dawn the young sun (बालसूर्यः) rises slowly (शनैः शनैः) out of the 'womb of the sea' (सागरगर्भात्). The water then turns golden (सुवर्णवर्णम्) and the sky becomes red (रक्तवर्णः). Travellers gather on the shore to watch this spectacle.
questions.explanation: Reproduces the imagery of the sunrise paragraph — the rising sun, golden water, red sky.

questions.question: चैत्रपूर्णिमायां कन्याकुमार्यां किम् अद्भुतं दृश्यं भवति? (What wondrous sight occurs at Kanyakumari on the Chaitra full moon?)
questions.answer: On the full-moon day of Chaitra (around April), the sun sets in one direction while, almost at the same time, the full moon rises in the opposite direction — both visible together from the same shore. Seeing the setting sun and the rising full moon over the sea at once, travellers are filled with amazement (विस्मिताः भवन्ति).
questions.explanation: The Chaitra-purnima spectacle: simultaneous sunset and moonrise seen from one shore.

questions.question: 'बालसूर्यः सागरगर्भात् उदेति' — अस्मिन् वाक्ये कवेः कल्पनाचातुर्यं (poetic imagination) विश्लेषयत।
questions.answer: The sentence personifies the sun as a child (बालसूर्यः, 'the infant sun') and pictures the sea as a mother whose womb (गर्भ) gives birth to him each morning. The rising of the sun over the horizon thus becomes a daily birth from the ocean. The metaphor conveys both the freshness and gentleness of the early sun (rising शनैः शनैः, slowly, like a child) and the traveller's sense of witnessing a living, wondrous event rather than a mere physical process.
questions.explanation: Literary appreciation: the metaphor of birth (सागरगर्भ) and the personification of the young sun.

questions.question: विवेकानन्दशिलायां किं स्मारकम् अस्ति? यात्रिकाः तत्र किम् अनुभवन्ति? (What memorial stands on the Vivekananda Rock, and what do visitors experience there?)
questions.answer: On the rock stands the grand Vivekananda Rock Memorial (भव्यं शिलास्मारकम्), built in 1970 in memory of Swami Vivekananda's meditation there. Visitors go to the rock by boats and experience peace (शान्तिम् अनुभवन्ति) in its meditation hall (ध्यानमण्डपम्).
questions.explanation: Recall of the memorial (1970), the boats, and the peace of the dhyana mandapam.

questions.question: कन्याकुमार्याः शिलायाः ध्यानं विवेकानन्दस्य जीवने कः परिवर्तनबिन्दुः (turning point) आसीत्? स्पष्टीकुरुत।
questions.answer: In December 1892 Vivekananda ended his long wandering across India at Kanyakumari. Swimming to the rock and meditating for three days, he reflected on India's condition and resolved to dedicate his life to the nation's uplift (भारतस्य उत्थानाय स्वजीवनं समर्पयितुं निश्चयम् अकरोत्). This resolve transformed the wandering monk into a man with a mission: the very next year (1893) he carried India's message to the World Parliament of Religions at Chicago. The rock thus marks the birthplace of his life's work.
questions.explanation: Analysis: connects the 1892 meditation, the resolve, and the 1893 Chicago address as cause and effect.

questions.question: विवेकानन्दविषये पाठात् चतुर्णां तथ्यानां (four facts) सूचीं कुरुत — वर्षसहितम्।
questions.answer: 1) In December 1892 he came to Kanyakumari after travelling across India. 2) He swam to the offshore rock and meditated there for three days. 3) On the rock he resolved to dedicate his life to India's uplift. 4) In 1893 he addressed the World Parliament of Religions at Chicago; the Rock Memorial in his memory was built in 1970.
questions.explanation: A structured recall of the key dated facts: 1892 meditation, three days, the resolve, 1893 Chicago, 1970 memorial.

questions.question: तिरुवल्लुवर-प्रतिमाविषये त्रीणि तथ्यानि लिखत। (Write three facts about the Thiruvalluvar statue.)
questions.answer: 1) It portrays the great Tamil poet Thiruvalluvar, author of the Tirukkural. 2) It is 133 feet (about 41 metres) tall — one foot for each of the Tirukkural's 133 chapters. 3) It stands on a rock in the sea near the Vivekananda Rock and was unveiled in the year 2000.
questions.explanation: Three recall facts: subject (Thiruvalluvar/Tirukkural), height (133 ft = 133 chapters), location and year (2000).

questions.question: 'दूरात् दृष्टा सा प्रतिमा धर्मस्य प्रहरी इव प्रतिभाति' — अस्य वाक्यस्य अनुवादं कृत्वा उपमायाः औचित्यं लिखत। (Translate the sentence and comment on the aptness of the simile.)
questions.answer: Translation: 'Seen from afar, that statue appears like a sentinel of dharma (standing in the sea).' The simile is apt because Thiruvalluvar's Tirukkural is a book of ethics (नीतिग्रन्थः) — a guide to righteous living. His towering figure facing the open ocean at India's gateway looks like a guard (प्रहरी) posted to protect dharma itself, as though righteousness keeps watch over the land from its southern tip.
questions.explanation: Translation plus literary appreciation of the प्रहरी simile connecting the poet's ethical work with the statue's guarding posture.

questions.question: तिरुक्कुरळ् कः ग्रन्थः? तस्मिन् कति अध्यायाः? (What kind of work is the Tirukkural, and how many chapters does it have?)
questions.answer: The Tirukkural is a celebrated Tamil book of ethics (नीतिग्रन्थः) composed by the poet-saint Thiruvalluvar. It contains 133 chapters (अध्यायाः) — the number honoured by the 133-foot height of his statue at Kanyakumari.
questions.explanation: Recall: genre (ethics), author (Thiruvalluvar), 133 chapters.

questions.question: नगरस्य नाम 'कन्याकुमारी' इति कथं सिद्धम्? देवीविषये जनश्रुतिं च लिखत। (How did the town get the name Kanyakumari? Also give the legend about the goddess.)
questions.answer: The town is named after Goddess Kanya Kumari, whose ancient temple stands on the sea-shore; devotees regard her as the maiden (कन्या) form of Parvati, and from her name (तस्याः नाम्ना एव) the town came to be called Kanyakumari. The legend (जनश्रुतिः) says her nose-ornament (नासाभरणम्) shone so brilliantly that its radiance was once seen even by boats sailing far out at sea.
questions.explanation: Etymology of the town's name from the goddess plus the nose-ornament legend.

questions.question: गान्धीमण्डपम् किम्? तत् कुत्र अस्ति? (What is the Gandhi Mandapam and where is it?)
questions.answer: The Gandhi Mandapam is a memorial to Mahatma Gandhi on the sea-shore at Kanyakumari (तटे एव). It marks the spot where Gandhi's ashes (भस्म) were kept before their immersion in the sea at the confluence.
questions.explanation: Recall from the temple paragraph: shore location, Gandhi's ashes kept there.

questions.question: सन्धि-विच्छेदं कृत्वा सन्धेः नाम लिखत: (a) सूर्यास्तः (b) चन्द्रोदयः (c) अतीव
questions.answer: (a) सूर्यास्तः = सूर्य + अस्तः — दीर्घ-सन्धिः (अ + अ = आ). (b) चन्द्रोदयः = चन्द्र + उदयः — गुण-सन्धिः (अ + उ = ओ). (c) अतीव = अति + इव — दीर्घ-सन्धिः (इ + इ = ई).
questions.explanation: Three sandhi splits from the lesson with the sandhi named: two दीर्घ and one गुण.

questions.question: अधोलिखितानां समासानां विग्रहं कृत्वा समासनाम लिखत: (a) देवीमन्दिरम् (b) बालसूर्यः (c) सागरत्रयसङ्गमः
questions.answer: (a) देवीमन्दिरम् = देव्याः मन्दिरम् — षष्ठी-तत्पुरुषः (the temple of the goddess). (b) बालसूर्यः = बालः च असौ सूर्यः च — कर्मधारयः (the young sun). (c) सागरत्रयसङ्गमः = सागरत्रयस्य सङ्गमः — षष्ठी-तत्पुरुषः, whose first member सागरत्रयम् (त्रयाणां सागराणां समाहारः) is a द्विगु compound.
questions.explanation: Compound analysis: two tatpurushas (one built on a dvigu) and one karmadharaya, all from the lesson.

questions.question: अधोलिखितेषु पदेषु कृत्-प्रत्ययं चिनुत, अर्थं च लिखत: दृष्ट्वा, उपगम्य, द्रष्टुम्, निर्मितम्, रमणीयम्।
questions.answer: दृष्ट्वा — क्त्वा, 'having seen'. उपगम्य — ल्यप् (absolutive with prefix उप), 'having approached'. द्रष्टुम् — तुमुन् (infinitive), 'to see'. निर्मितम् — क्त (past passive participle), 'built'. रमणीयम् — अनीयर् (potential participle), 'delightful / worth enjoying'.
questions.explanation: Identification of five कृदन्त forms spanning क्त्वा, ल्यप्, तुमुन्, क्त and अनीयर्.

questions.question: Translate into English: 'देश-विदेशेभ्यः सहस्रशः यात्रिकाः प्रतिदिनम् अत्र आगच्छन्ति।'
questions.answer: Every day thousands of travellers (pilgrims) come here from India and abroad (literally: from their own country and foreign countries).
questions.explanation: देश-विदेशेभ्यः = from home and foreign lands (पञ्चमी); सहस्रशः = in thousands; प्रतिदिनम् = every day.

questions.question: Give the शब्दार्थ of: सङ्गमस्थानम्, वर्णभेदः, स्मृत्यर्थम्, अनावृता, प्रहरी.
questions.answer: सङ्गमस्थानम् = meeting place, confluence; वर्णभेदः = difference of colour; स्मृत्यर्थम् = in memory (of), for the sake of remembrance; अनावृता = unveiled; प्रहरी = sentinel, watchman.
questions.explanation: Five vocabulary items drawn from different paragraphs of the prose.

questions.question: Translate into Sanskrit (Devanagari): (a) Three seas meet at Kanyakumari. (b) Travellers see the sunrise. (c) The statue shines in the sea.
questions.answer: (a) कन्याकुमार्यां त्रयः सागराः मिलन्ति। (b) यात्रिकाः सूर्योदयं पश्यन्ति। (c) प्रतिमा सागरे राजते।
questions.explanation: Simple English-to-Sanskrit rendering using chapter vocabulary: मिलन्ति, पश्यन्ति, राजते; locatives कन्याकुमार्याम्, सागरे.

questions.question: यात्रावर्णनम् (travel description) किम्? अस्य पाठस्य आधारेण यात्रावर्णनस्य त्रीणि लक्षणानि सोदाहरणं लिखत। (What is a travel description? With examples from this lesson, state three features of the form.)
questions.answer: A यात्रावर्णनम् is a prose composition in which the author describes a journey — the places seen, their sights, history and atmosphere — so vividly that the reader feels present there. Three features, with examples from this lesson: (1) Vivid word-painting of nature: the young sun rising from the 'womb of the sea' (बालसूर्यः सागरगर्भात् उदेति), the golden water and red sky, the foamy waves whose roar is heard from afar. (2) Weaving in of history, legend and culture: Vivekananda's three-day meditation of December 1892 and the 1970 memorial; the Tirukkural's 133 chapters matched by the 133-foot statue; the legend of the Devi's shining nose-ornament. (3) The traveller's own feeling and reflection: the amazement (विस्मिताः) at the Chaitra full-moon spectacle and the closing reflection that Kanyakumari is a symbol of India's unity, summed up in the refrain राजते खलु कन्याकुमारी. Together these make the reader a fellow-traveller rather than a mere reader of facts.
questions.explanation: Defines the genre and grounds three of its features (imagery, history/legend, personal reflection) in the text.

questions.question: सागरत्रयसङ्गमस्य वर्णनं पाठानुसारं विस्तरेण कुरुत — के सागराः, कासु दिक्षु, किं च तत्र आश्चर्यम्? (Describe the confluence of the three seas in detail — which seas, in which directions, and what is wondrous there?)
questions.answer: Kanyakumari is the meeting place (सङ्गमस्थानम्) of three seas: in the east the Bay of Bengal (बङ्गोपसागरः), in the west the Arabian Sea (अरबसागरः), and in the south the vast Indian Ocean (हिन्दमहासागरः). Because three waters meet, the confluence is called त्रिवेणीसङ्गमः, on the model of the three-river confluence at Prayag. The wonders of the place are several: standing on the shore one can actually see the difference in the colours of the waters (जलानां वर्णभेदः) of the three seas; the waves strike the shore and turn foamy (फेनिलाः), and their roar (घोषः) is heard even from afar; and devotees believe that bathing at the confluence bestows merit (सङ्गमस्नानं पुण्यप्रदम्). The confluence also carries a deeper meaning in the lesson: as three seas merge into one, so the many cultures of India merge at Kanyakumari — making the spot both a natural marvel and a symbol of unity.
questions.explanation: Full description: three seas with directions, the Triveni name, colour difference, foamy roaring waves, the bathing belief, and the symbolic reading.

questions.question: कन्याकुमार्याः सूर्योदय-सूर्यास्तयोः वर्णनं पाठात् उद्धृत्य लिखत, तथा च विश्लेषयत — लेखकः वर्णैः (colours) उपमाभिः च कथं चित्रम् इव रचयति?
questions.answer: Description: In the early morning the young sun (बालसूर्यः) rises slowly, slowly (शनैः शनैः) from the womb of the sea (सागरगर्भात्); the water turns golden (सुवर्णवर्णम्) and the sky red (रक्तवर्णः). In the evening the same sun seems to sink (मज्जति इव) into the western sea. Uniquely, both sunrise and sunset can be watched from the same shore — the विशेषता of Kanyakumari — and on the Chaitra full moon the setting sun and the rising full moon appear together in opposite directions, leaving travellers amazed. Analysis: the author paints like a painter — laying on colours (golden water, red sky, the white foam of the waves), personifying the sun as a newborn child emerging from the sea's womb, and using इव-similes (मज्जति इव, 'as if diving') to turn physical events into living actions. The slow rhythm of शनैः शनैः imitates the sun's gradual rise. Through colour, personification and simile the prose becomes a word-picture (शब्दचित्रम्) that lets the reader see the scene.
questions.explanation: Combines faithful description with literary analysis of colour imagery, personification and simile.

questions.question: 'विवेकानन्दशिला केवलं शिला न, अपि तु प्रेरणास्थानम्' — इति कथनं पाठाधारेण समर्थयत। (Support this statement — 'The Vivekananda Rock is not merely a rock but a place of inspiration' — from the lesson.)
questions.answer: The statement is fully justified. Physically the rock is only a mass of stone in the sea near the shore; its greatness comes from what happened on it. In December 1892 Swami Vivekananda, having wandered across the whole of India and seen her poverty and glory, swam through the sea, sat on this rock and meditated for three days. There he took the resolve that shaped modern Indian history — to dedicate his life to the uplift of India (भारतस्य उत्थानाय). Strengthened by that resolve, he carried India's spiritual message to the World Parliament of Religions at Chicago in 1893 and awakened the world's respect for Indian culture. The nation acknowledged the rock's power of inspiration by building the grand Rock Memorial there in 1970; even today pilgrims cross by boat and sit in its dhyana mandapam, where they experience peace (शान्तिम् अनुभवन्ति) and are silently invited to make their own resolves. A rock that turned a wandering monk into a world teacher, and that still turns tourists into meditators, is truly a प्रेरणास्थानम् — a place of inspiration, not mere stone.
questions.explanation: Evaluative essay: the 1892 meditation, the resolve, the 1893 Chicago mission, the 1970 memorial and the continuing experience of peace.

questions.question: तिरुवल्लुवरस्य प्रतिमायाः विषये पाठाधारेण निबन्धं लिखत — कविः, ग्रन्थः, प्रतिमायाः वैशिष्ट्यम्, अनावरणवर्षं च। (Write an essay on the Thiruvalluvar statue — the poet, his work, the statue's special features and the year of unveiling.)
questions.answer: The poet: Thiruvalluvar is a revered poet-saint of the Tamil language (तमिळमहाकविः), honoured across India as a teacher of ethics. His work: he composed the Tirukkural (तिरुक्कुरळ्), a नीतिग्रन्थः — a classic of right conduct — arranged in 133 chapters, whose short couplets guide life in virtue, wealth and love. The statue: on a rock in the sea near the Vivekananda Rock stands his lofty (उत्तुङ्गा) stone statue. Its most striking feature is its height — 133 feet (about 41 metres), one foot for every chapter of the Tirukkural, so that the monument's very measurements honour the book. Seen from afar, the statue appears like a sentinel of dharma (धर्मस्य प्रहरी इव) keeping watch over India's southern gateway. Unveiling: the statue was unveiled to the public in the year 2000. Standing beside the memorial of Vivekananda, the Tamil poet's statue makes Kanyakumari a meeting place not only of seas but of India's literary and spiritual traditions.
questions.explanation: Essay organised around the four asked points: poet, Tirukkural (133 chapters), 133-foot statue with the प्रहरी simile, unveiled 2000.

questions.question: 'कन्याकुमारी भारतस्य एकतायाः प्रतीकम्' — पाठस्य उपसंहारम् आधारीकृत्य एतत् कथनं विस्तरेण विवेचयत, स्वमतम् अपि लिखत।
questions.answer: The conclusion of the lesson states that Kanyakumari is not merely a place of natural beauty (प्रकृतिसौन्दर्यस्य स्थानम्) but a symbol of India's unity (एकतायाः प्रतीकम्). The claim rests on a beautiful parallel: just as three different seas — the Bay of Bengal, the Arabian Sea and the Indian Ocean — merge into one confluence here, so do the different streams of Indian culture. On this one shore stand together the ancient temple of a southern goddess (देवी कन्याकुमारी, the maiden form of Parvati), the 133-foot statue of the Tamil poet Thiruvalluvar, the memorial of Swami Vivekananda — a monk born in Bengal in India's east — and the Gandhi Mandapam recalling the father of the nation. South and east, goddess and poet and monk, devotion, literature and patriotism all meet at one point, and pilgrims from every state stand shoulder to shoulder watching the same sunrise. In my view the symbolism is apt and instructive: it teaches that India's diversity, like the three seas, does not divide but merges into one grandeur. A visit to Kanyakumari is thus a lesson in national integration — and every visitor may rightly exclaim, राजते खलु कन्याकुमारी!
questions.explanation: Evaluative essay on the unity theme: the sea-simile, the four monuments of different regions/traditions, and a reasoned personal opinion.

questions.question: अस्मात् पाठात् व्याकरणसामग्रीं सङ्कलय्य लिखत — (a) द्वे सन्धि-उदाहरणे सविच्छेदम्, (b) द्वौ समासौ सविग्रहम्, (c) चत्वारि कृदन्तपदानि सप्रत्ययम्, (d) तिसृणां विभक्तीनाम् एकैकम् उदाहरणम्।
questions.answer: (a) सन्धिः: सूर्योदयः = सूर्य + उदयः (गुण-सन्धिः, अ + उ = ओ); अतीव = अति + इव (दीर्घ-सन्धिः, इ + इ = ई). (b) समासः: सागरत्रयसङ्गमः = सागरत्रयस्य सङ्गमः (षष्ठी-तत्पुरुषः, built on the द्विगु सागरत्रयम्); बालसूर्यः = बालः च असौ सूर्यः च (कर्मधारयः). (c) कृदन्ताः: दृष्ट्वा — क्त्वा ('having seen'); उपगम्य — ल्यप् ('having approached', prefix उप); द्रष्टुम् — तुमुन् ('to see'); निर्मितम् — क्त ('was built'). One may add रमणीयम् — अनीयर् ('worth enjoying'). (d) विभक्तयः: तृतीया — नौकाभिः ('by boats'); पञ्चमी — तटात् ('from the shore'); सप्तमी — मन्दिरे ('in the temple') or शिलायाम् ('on the rock'). Such collection shows how the travel prose itself becomes a grammar textbook: every paragraph yields sandhis, compounds, participles and case-forms in living use.
questions.explanation: A consolidated grammar harvest from the passage: 2 sandhis, 2 compounds, 4+ kridantas with suffixes, and 3 case examples.

questions.question: भवान्/भवती कन्याकुमारीं दृष्टवान्/दृष्टवती इति कल्पयित्वा पञ्चवाक्यात्मकम् अनुच्छेदं संस्कृतेन लिखत (सूर्योदयः, सागरत्रयम्, शिला, प्रतिमा, मन्दिरं च उल्लेख्यम्), आङ्ग्लानुवादं च ददत।
questions.answer: Model answer: अहं गतवर्षे कन्याकुमारीं गतवान्। प्रातःकाले तटे स्थित्वा अहं सागरगर्भात् उदयन्तं बालसूर्यम् अपश्यम्। तत्र त्रयः सागराः मिलन्ति, जलानां वर्णभेदः च दृश्यते। नौकया गत्वा अहं विवेकानन्दशिलायां ध्यानमण्डपे शान्तिम् अन्वभवम्, समीपे च तिरुवल्लुवरस्य उत्तुङ्गां प्रतिमाम् अपश्यम्। अन्ते देव्याः कन्याकुमार्याः प्राचीनं मन्दिरं प्रणम्य अहम् अवदम् — राजते खलु कन्याकुमारी! Translation: Last year I went to Kanyakumari. Standing on the shore in the early morning, I saw the young sun rising from the womb of the sea. There three seas meet, and the difference in the colours of the waters is visible. Going by boat, I experienced peace in the meditation hall on the Vivekananda Rock, and nearby I saw the lofty statue of Thiruvalluvar. Finally, bowing at the ancient temple of Devi Kanya Kumari, I said — Kanyakumari shines indeed!
questions.explanation: A CREATE-level composition task; the model paragraph uses chapter vocabulary, absolutives (स्थित्वा, गत्वा, प्रणम्य) and covers all five required items.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer:
'भारतवर्षस्य दक्षिणतमे प्रान्ते तमिळनाडुराज्ये कन्याकुमारी नाम विश्वविश्रुतं नगरम् अस्ति। इदं स्थलं भारतमातुः चरणतीर्थम् इति कविभिः वर्ण्यते, यतः अत्र एव भारतभूमिः समाप्यते, सागरः च आरभ्यते।'
(a) कन्याकुमारी कस्मिन् राज्ये अस्ति? (b) 'विश्वविश्रुतम्' इत्यस्य अर्थः कः? (c) कवयः इदं स्थलं किम् इति वर्णयन्ति, किमर्थं च?
questions.answer: (a) कन्याकुमारी तमिळनाडुराज्ये अस्ति — in the state of Tamil Nadu. (b) विश्वविश्रुतम् = world-famous, renowned throughout the world (विश्व + विश्रुत 'heard of everywhere'). (c) Poets describe it as भारतमातुः चरणतीर्थम् — the holy place at Mother India's feet — because here the land of India ends (समाप्यते) and the ocean begins (आरभ्यते): it is the southernmost point of the mainland.
questions.explanation: Comprehension of the opening paragraph: state, meaning of the epithet विश्वविश्रुतम्, and the reason for the चरणतीर्थ image.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer:
'पूर्वस्यां दिशि बङ्गोपसागरः, पश्चिमायां दिशि अरबसागरः, दक्षिणस्यां दिशि च विशालः हिन्दमहासागरः — एते त्रयः सागराः अत्र परस्परं मिलन्ति। अयं सङ्गमः त्रिवेणीसङ्गमः इति अपि कथ्यते।'
(a) दक्षिणस्यां दिशि कः सागरः? (b) 'परस्परम्' इत्यस्य अर्थः कः? (c) अयं सङ्गमः केन नाम्ना अपि कथ्यते?
questions.answer: (a) दक्षिणस्यां दिशि विशालः हिन्दमहासागरः अस्ति — the vast Indian Ocean lies to the south. (b) परस्परम् = mutually, with one another; the three seas meet one another. (c) The confluence is also called त्रिवेणीसङ्गमः (Triveni Sangam).
questions.explanation: Direct comprehension of the confluence passage: direction of the Indian Ocean, meaning of परस्परम्, and the alternate name.

questions.question:
Read and answer:
'आश्चर्यम् इदं यत् त्रयाणां सागराणां जलानां वर्णभेदः अपि तटे स्थित्वा द्रष्टुं शक्यते। तरङ्गाः तटम् आहत्य फेनिलाः भवन्ति; तेषां घोषः दूरात् अपि श्रूयते।'
(a) किम् 'आश्चर्यम्' इति उक्तम्? (b) 'स्थित्वा' 'आहत्य' इति पदयोः प्रत्ययौ लिखत। (c) 'श्रूयते' — अत्र कः प्रयोगः (कर्तरि/कर्मणि)? अर्थं च लिखत।
questions.answer: (a) The wonder is that, standing on the shore, one can see even the difference in the colours of the waters (जलानां वर्णभेदः) of the three seas. (b) स्थित्वा — क्त्वा प्रत्ययः (स्था + क्त्वा, 'having stood'); आहत्य — ल्यप् प्रत्ययः (आ + हन् + ल्यप्, 'having struck', because of the prefix आ). (c) श्रूयते is कर्मणि प्रयोगः (passive voice) of श्रु — 'is heard'; the roar of the waves is heard even from afar.
questions.explanation: Combines comprehension (the wonder) with grammar: क्त्वा vs ल्यप् and recognition of the passive श्रूयते.

questions.question:
Read and answer:
'चैत्रपूर्णिमायां तु अद्भुतं दृश्यं भवति — एकस्यां दिशि सूर्यः अस्तं गच्छति, अन्यस्यां दिशि च पूर्णचन्द्रः उदेति। एतत् दृश्यं दृष्ट्वा यात्रिकाः विस्मिताः भवन्ति।'
(a) अद्भुतं दृश्यं किम्? (b) 'पूर्णिमायाम्' इति पदे का विभक्तिः, कः अर्थः? (c) 'दृष्ट्वा' इति कीदृशं पदम्? (d) यात्रिकाः कीदृशाः भवन्ति?
questions.answer: (a) The wondrous sight is that on the Chaitra full moon the sun sets in one direction while the full moon rises in the other — both at nearly the same time. (b) पूर्णिमायाम् is सप्तमी विभक्तिः (locative), expressing time — 'on the full-moon day'. (c) दृष्ट्वा is a क्त्वा-प्रत्ययान्तं कृदन्तपदम् (absolutive) — 'having seen'. (d) यात्रिकाः विस्मिताः भवन्ति — the travellers become amazed, filled with wonder.
questions.explanation: Comprehension of the full-moon spectacle plus grammar: locative of time, the absolutive दृष्ट्वा, and the क्त form विस्मिताः.

questions.question:
Read and answer:
'१८९२ तमे ख्रिष्टाब्दे दिसम्बरमासे स्वामी विवेकानन्दः भारतभ्रमणं समाप्य अत्र आगतः। सः सागरं तीर्त्वा तां शिलाम् उपगम्य त्रिदिनं ध्यानम् अकरोत्। तत्र एव सः भारतस्य उत्थानाय स्वजीवनं समर्पयितुं निश्चयम् अकरोत्।'
(a) विवेकानन्दः कदा कन्याकुमारीम् आगतः? (b) सः शिलायां किं किम् अकरोत्? (c) 'समर्पयितुम्' इति पदे कः प्रत्ययः?
questions.answer: (a) He came to Kanyakumari in December 1892 (१८९२ तमे ख्रिष्टाब्दे दिसम्बरमासे), after completing his journey across India. (b) On the rock he meditated for three days (त्रिदिनं ध्यानम् अकरोत्) and there resolved to dedicate his life to India's uplift (निश्चयम् अकरोत्). (c) समर्पयितुम् has the तुमुन् प्रत्ययः — the infinitive 'to dedicate'.
questions.explanation: Comprehension of the Vivekananda paragraph with one grammar point (तुमुन् infinitive).

questions.question:
Read and answer:
'ततः परं सः १८९३ तमे वर्षे चिकागोनगरे विश्वधर्मसम्मेलने भारतीयसंस्कृतेः सन्देशं जगते अददात्। तस्य स्मृत्यर्थं १९७० तमे वर्षे तस्यां शिलायां भव्यं शिलास्मारकं निर्मितम्।'
(a) १८९३ तमे वर्षे किम् अभवत्? (b) 'जगते' इति पदे का विभक्तिः, किमर्थं प्रयुक्ता? (c) कन्याकुमारीध्यानस्य चिकागोभाषणस्य च कः सम्बन्धः इति विश्लेषयत।
questions.answer: (a) In 1893 Vivekananda gave the message of Indian culture to the world at the World Parliament of Religions in Chicago. (b) जगते is चतुर्थी विभक्तिः (dative) — the message was given TO the world; the dative marks the recipient of the verb अददात् ('gave'). (c) The two events are cause and effect: the resolve born during the three-day meditation on the Kanyakumari rock (December 1892) — to dedicate his life to India's uplift — gave Vivekananda his mission and confidence; the Chicago address of 1893 was the first great fulfilment of that resolve, carrying India's spiritual message abroad. The rock supplied the inner decision; Chicago was its outer expression.
questions.explanation: Comprehension plus the dative of recipient and a cause-effect analysis linking 1892 meditation to the 1893 address.

questions.question:
Read and answer:
'तिरुवल्लुवरः तिरुक्कुरळ् इति नीतिग्रन्थस्य रचयिता। तस्मिन् ग्रन्थे १३३ अध्यायाः सन्ति; अतः एव प्रतिमायाः औच्च्यम् अपि १३३ पादमितम् अस्ति। इयं शिलाप्रतिमा २००० तमे ख्रिष्टाब्दे जनसामान्याय अनावृता।'
(a) तिरुक्कुरळ्-ग्रन्थे कति अध्यायाः? (b) प्रतिमायाः औच्च्यं किमर्थं १३३ पादमितम्? (c) 'जनसामान्याय अनावृता' इत्यस्य अर्थं लिखत।
questions.answer: (a) The Tirukkural has 133 chapters (अध्यायाः). (b) The statue's height was made exactly 133 feet so that it would match the number of chapters of the Tirukkural — the monument's measurements honour the book (अतः एव, 'for that very reason'). (c) जनसामान्याय अनावृता = 'was unveiled for the general public' — in the year 2000 the statue was formally opened for all people to see (जनसामान्याय is dative: for the common people).
questions.explanation: Comprehension of the statue paragraph: 133 chapters, the reason for the 133-foot height, and the dative phrase of unveiling.

questions.question:
Read and answer:
'सागरतटे देव्याः कन्याकुमार्याः प्राचीनं मन्दिरम् अस्ति। तस्याः देव्याः नाम्ना एव अस्य नगरस्य नाम कन्याकुमारी इति अभवत्। देव्याः नासाभरणं तथा दीप्यते यत् तस्य प्रभा पुरा सागरे दूरं गच्छन्तीभिः नौकाभिः अपि दृश्यते स्म इति जनश्रुतिः।'
(a) मन्दिरं कुत्र अस्ति? (b) नगरस्य नाम कथम् अभवत्? (c) नासाभरणविषये का जनश्रुतिः?
questions.answer: (a) The ancient temple stands on the sea-shore (सागरतटे). (b) The town's name arose from the name of the goddess herself (तस्याः देव्याः नाम्ना एव) — it is called Kanyakumari after Devi Kanya Kumari. (c) The legend is that the goddess's nose-ornament (नासाभरणम्) shines so brightly that in earlier times its radiance (प्रभा) was seen even by boats sailing far out at sea.
questions.explanation: Comprehension of the temple paragraph: location, etymology of the town's name, and the nose-ornament legend.

questions.question:
Read the sentence and answer the grammar questions:
'अद्य यात्रिकाः नौकाभिः तत्र गत्वा ध्यानमण्डपे शान्तिम् अनुभवन्ति।'
(a) 'नौकाभिः' — विभक्तिं वचनं च लिखत। (b) 'गत्वा' — प्रत्ययं मूलधातुं च लिखत। (c) 'ध्यानमण्डपे' — विभक्तिं लिखत, समासविग्रहं च कुरुत। (d) वाक्यस्य आङ्ग्लानुवादं कुरुत।
questions.answer: (a) नौकाभिः — तृतीया विभक्तिः, बहुवचनम् ('by boats', instrumental plural of नौका). (b) गत्वा — क्त्वा प्रत्ययः, मूलधातुः गम् ('having gone'). (c) ध्यानमण्डपे — सप्तमी विभक्तिः ('in the meditation hall'); विग्रहः — ध्यानस्य मण्डपम् = ध्यानमण्डपम् (षष्ठी-तत्पुरुषः), 'the hall for meditation'. (d) Translation: Today travellers, going there by boats, experience peace in the meditation hall.
questions.explanation: A grammar case-study on one sentence: instrumental plural, क्त्वा absolutive, locative with compound analysis, and translation.

questions.question:
Read the concluding passage and answer:
'कन्याकुमारी केवलं प्रकृतिसौन्दर्यस्य स्थानं न, अपि तु भारतस्य एकतायाः प्रतीकम् अपि। अत्र दक्षिणस्य देवीमन्दिरम्, तमिळकवेः प्रतिमा, बङ्गप्रदेशस्य संन्यासिनः स्मारकं च एकत्र मिलन्ति — यथा त्रयः सागराः एकत्र मिलन्ति तथा।'
(a) Translate the second sentence into English. (b) 'संन्यासिनः' कः अत्र निर्दिष्टः? (c) Do you find the comparison (यथा...तथा) effective? Give one reason.
questions.answer: (a) Translation: 'Here the temple of the goddess of the south, the statue of the Tamil poet, and the memorial of the monk of Bengal meet in one place — just as the three seas meet in one place.' (b) The monk (संन्यासी) referred to is Swami Vivekananda, who was born in Bengal (Calcutta) and whose memorial stands on the rock. (c) Yes, the comparison is effective. One strong reason: it grounds an abstract idea (national unity) in a visible natural fact — the visitor literally SEES three seas merging before his eyes, and the simile invites him to see India's cultures merging in the same way, making the message concrete and memorable.
questions.explanation: Translation, identification of Vivekananda as the Bengal monk, and an evaluated judgement on the simile of the merging seas.
